title: KV eviction safety: fuzzbench harness for prefix-cohesion and GPU fragmentation
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We need a reproducible harness that validates eviction invariants across hybrid LRU+TTL heuristics, prefix-aware pinning, and GPU memory fragmentation scenarios that arise from continuous batching. This ticket builds a fuzzbench-style simulator and an on-device smoke runner to catch correctness regressions (stale KV reads, partial-prefix evictions, and in-flight eviction races) before changes roll to canary clusters.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible fuzzbench harness exists that models request arrival distributions, prefix affinity, and batch coalescing (sampling knobs exposed),

A set of formal invariants are encoded as checks: (1) prefix-cohesion: no request observes a partial eviction for prefixes pinned by that request; (2) in-flight immunity: a request that started while a slot was still allocated must not read an evicted entry; (3) monotonicity: once a prefix is unpinned and later evicted, subsequent fetches behave as cache-miss until repopulation,
>95% of random seeds that previously triggered flaky edge failures are now covered by at least one failing seed in the harness,
A CI job runs a targeted subset of the harness on PRs modifying eviction logic, and a nightly stronger-suite runs longer seeds,
Bench artifacts (traces, failing seeds, heap/gpu snapshots) are automatically uploaded to the artifact store and linked in the ticket for any failing run.
implementation_notes: Harness design: two components — (1) offline simulator with configurable knobs (arrival distribution, batching window, prefix skew-factor, TTL distribution, slab fragmentation) written in Go to mirror runtime allocation policies, (2) lightweight on-device runner that replays failing seeds against a dev-gpu instance to validate real-memory behavior.

Eviction policy under test: hybrid LRU + TTL weighted by prefix priority. Introduce an eviction fence per-prefix: fence transitions allow in-flight requests to complete before reclamation. Fencing is implemented as an atomic compare-and-swap on slot state + epoch counter.

Correctness invariants: prefix atomicity (prefix pinned/unpinned as a single logical op), read-after-evict safety (requests in the same batch must be evaluated against the pre-eviction view), and slot re-use sanitation (KV slot zeroization before reuse on GPU to avoid cross-tenant leakage).

Trade-offs considered: stronger fencing increases live-memory and can raise tail latency under high pressure; we expose a fence-timeout knob and plan to tune per-tenant via Dedicated capacity settings. We prioritized correctness first for canary and then will iterate on shorter fence windows to recover memory efficiency.
test_plan: Phase 1 (dev): run 10k short seeds locally (0.1s-30s) to surface fast regressions; failing seeds are stored with heap/gpu snapshot.
Phase 2 (CI): run reduced harness on PRs that touch eviction/slot code. If any invariant fails, block merge.
Phase 3 (staging): nightly long seeds (1M events) run on a staging GPU cluster to reproduce fragmentation and long-ttl interactions; compare cache-hit histograms vs. baseline.
Phase 4 (on-device validation): replay selected failing seeds on a dev-box with "--replay-real-memory" to ensure the simulator failure corresponds to an actual GPU memory behavior.
benchmarks_and_results: Initial fuzzbench run (seed corpus v1): 50k seeds, workload skew 0.75, median cache-hit delta vs baseline: -0.6pp, 99th percentile eviction-safety violations: 0 -> 3 before fixes, now 0 after fence implementation,

On-device replay of representative failing seed: reproduced stale read where a request observed a partially-evicted prefix (root cause: racing slot free + batch coalescer). Fix: added per-prefix epoch and eviction-fence; replay after fix shows no stale reads over 200k replayed requests.
Perf impact: fence adds 1.9% median token-latency in synthetic tight-memory microbench with extreme pinning; acceptable for correctness gating in canary.
rollback_playbook: If canary shows increased eviction-safety violations or customer-visible errors, immediately revert the eviction runtime change via runtime-1.22 rollback tag,
Isolate by toggling runtime feature-flag: runtime.kv.eviction.fence_enabled=false, and re-run failing seeds,
Notify SRE and engaged customers via incident channel and open a postmortem if customer-facing errors observed.
updates: 2026-03-02: initial prototype simulator done (Sofia). Exposed knobs: prefix-skew, batch-window-ms, ttl-mean, slab-count.

2026-03-04: found reproducible seed that triggers partial-prefix visibility during heavy batching (Arjun). Root cause traced to slot free happening before batch commit, added epoch counter memoization as workaround.

2026-03-07: implemented eviction-fence (epoch + CAS) in runtime, unit tests added. Perf microbench shows 1.9% median latency regression under contrived stress; acceptable for canary gating. PR opened: #7342.
2026-03-09: CI harness integrated into PR pipeline for eviction-related PRs. Nightly long-suite scheduled (window 02:00 UTC).
2026-03-13: on-device replay validated a previously flaky seed; no stale reads after fence. Preparing canary rollout plan and telemetry thresholds.
next_steps: Finish CI optimization so PR-level runs finish within 12m (current median 28m),
Add more realistic client traces to seed corpus (ingest from prod scrubbed traces),
Coordinate with Dedicated team to expose fence-timeout as per-tenant knob and run a small Dedicated canary with 5 customers.
